skills.content:
---
name: ascii-music-video
description: >-
  Use when someone wants to turn a song (MP3 plus optional lyrics) into a
  beat-synced ASCII-art music video.
---
Turn a song into a beat-synced ASCII / glyph / dot-art music video. Scenes come from the lyrics, images are generated per scene, and the camera motion follows the beat.

## Inputs
- MP3 (required). Suno blocks downloads from share links, so ask the user to export it: open the song on suno.com, use the "..." menu, choose Download, then MP3 Audio, and upload the file here.
- Lyrics (optional). A pasted lyrics .txt, or the Suno song link (lyrics and genre tags; read them from the public page). Keep Suno's [Verse]/[Hook] tags. Without lyrics, transcribe.
- Theme / style hint (optional). If the user names one, it wins.
- User photos (optional): use as the image for the best-fitting scene, padded to 16:9; never generate images of a real person.

## Steps
1. Engine. `git clone https://github.com/ecoay/ascii-music-video && cd ascii-music-video && bash setup.sh`. If git is missing: `curl -L https://codeload.github.com/ecoay/ascii-music-video/tar.gz/refs/heads/main | tar xz && cd ascii-music-video-main && bash setup.sh`. First run takes ~2-5 min.
2. Plan. `.venv/bin/python plan_scenes.py song.mp3 [--lyrics lyrics.txt] --target 14 --out scenes`. Check the match % and scene list; fix any scene that is absurdly short or long (use beat section breaks) or adjust `--target`.
3. Discover the visual style. Unless the user gave one, derive a single art style for the whole video from the song itself: genre and Suno style tags, tempo and energy, mood, era, setting and imagery in the lyrics (e.g. lo-fi ballad becomes soft watercolor or film-grain photography; trap anthem becomes chrome and neon street noir; folk becomes woodcut or ink etching; synthwave becomes retro 80s airbrush; metal becomes dark engraving). Pick a medium, palette and lighting, state it in one line to the user with the preview, and keep it consistent across scenes. Do not default to one house style for every song.
4. Prompts. For each entry in `scenes/image_prompts.json`, write a prompt depicting what the lyric means (the metaphor) in the chosen style. One clear subject; end every prompt with: "<chosen style>, dark, high-contrast, single centered subject on pure black background, hard rim light, bold silhouette, no text." (The black background and contrast keep it readable as ASCII.)
5. Images. Generate each with your image tool (16:9), resize to 1920x1080, save as `scenes/scene_NN.png`.
6. Preview. `.venv/bin/python asciimv.py song.mp3 --scenes-json scenes/scenes.json --style auto --skyline --lyrics-overlay -o video.mp4 --stills-only --still <mid-scene times>`.
   - Motion: circular objects spin to tempo; distant/detailed subjects get a zoom-through landing on the downbeat; others pan/bounce with kick cuts.
   - Style: colorful goes color, dark goes dots, else glow/binary.
   - If a subject doesn't read, set "style":"dots" or tweak cell/gain; if zoom turns it to a blob, use pan.
7. Send the best preview still first, with the one-line style choice.
8. Render the full video (same command without --stills-only; ~2x song length on CPU). Make the X copy: `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 20 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart video_x.mp4`. Chat attachments cap at 200 MB, so if larger, re-encode at ~3400k video bitrate before sending.

## Revisions
- Change the overall style: pick a new one, rewrite all prompts, regenerate.
- Swap an image: rewrite the prompt, regenerate, re-render.
- Per scene: "style" glow|color|dots|binary; "cell"; "gain"; "motion" spin|zoom|pan; "focus":[x,y]; "spin_circle":[cx,cy,r]; "spin_zoom".
- Timing: edit scene start values or re-plan with a different --target.
- Toggles: drop --lyrics-overlay or --skyline.
- Always preview with --stills-only before a full re-render. Never post anywhere for the user; just hand over the files.

skills.name: ascii-music-video-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the ASCII music video bot.
skills.content:
---
name: ascii-music-video-getting-started
description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the ASCII music video bot.
---
Start with one line: "I turn your song into a beat-synced ASCII-art music video, with scenes drawn from your lyrics and everything cut to the beat."

Then ask, one question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. "Upload the song as an MP3. From Suno, open the song, use the ... menu, then Download, then MP3 Audio. Share links won't download."
2. "Got lyrics? Paste them, upload a .txt, or send the Suno song link. Or say 'transcribe' and I'll pull them from the audio."
3. "Want a particular look, or should I pick a style that fits the song? Want any of your own photos in the video? Upload them."

Then run the ascii-music-video skill. Keep the user posted (setting up, planning scenes, picking the style, making images, here's a preview frame). Send the preview still before the full render, then deliver the MP4 plus an X-ready copy and offer revisions.
